“Not set by the size of the tissue” is formalised as “determined by du, dv and det J alone” (a uniqueness statement). That is an argument from the absence of a variable, which is weaker than an independence proof: it shows the onset RELATION cannot depend on tissue size, not that the mechanism cannot. This is the single weakest link in the law and the proposer wants it attacked directly.

On a finite domain the admissible modes ARE quantised by the boundary conditions, so the realised spacing does depend on tissue size. The scope sentence says so. Decide whether a law whose headline reads “not by the size of the tissue” should be allowed to carry that caveat only in scope.

The scaling conjunct (qm*m = q under uniform diffusivity rescaling) is exact and is the law’s strongest content, but it is stated only for m > 1. The m < 1 case follows by symmetry and is not stated. Check whether that was laziness or a mutation-test artefact.

The witness (du = 1, dv = 4, Dt = 4, q = 1) is illustrative, with no source, and its diffusivity ratio (4) is far below the turing-ddi witness ratio (40). Decide whether two witnesses of sibling laws should be mutually consistent.
EVALUABLE-BUT-UNSUPPLIABLE: TURINGLAMBDA1 needs a critical wavenumber, two diffusivities and a kinetic Jacobian, none of which any design carries.
This law and turing-ddi share the same hypothesis family and the same missing inputs. Argue whether they should be one law with two conjuncts rather than two laws.
